key_insight: Calibration-aware reinforcement learning can route quantum circuits to higher exact fidelity by avoiding poorly calibrated couplers, even when that increases two-qubit gate count.
engineering_relevance: For NISQ compilers, using same-day hardware calibration data in routing decisions can improve run quality beyond standard gate-count minimization.
method: Graph RL router with proximal policy optimization
Uses IBM Heron r2 same-day calibration snapshots as edge features
Compared against SABRE-best20 and target-aware SABRE on MQT Bench circuits
evidence_signal: Across nine MQT Bench circuits and three calibration snapshots, pooled mean exact fidelity was 0.727 versus 0.440 for SABRE-best20 and 0.481 for target-aware SABRE.
watch_item: The gains come with higher routed two-qubit counts, and under the fixed tree action graph the 10q families still favor SABRE-best20, so the approach may not generalize uniformly.
paper_title: Graph Reinforcement Learning for Calibration-Aware Quantum Circuit Routing
